name: B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering
duration_note: A full four-year professional engineering degree including workshop training, CAD design, farm machinery field operation, hydrological modeling, and in-plant industrial training under ICAR's Student READY component in the final year.

hero.summary: A four-year engineering programme applying mechanical, civil, electrical, and data engineering principles to farm mechanisation, micro-irrigation, post-harvest processing, renewable energy, and precision agriculture technologies like drones and IoT.

overview.heading: What the B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering degree covers
paragraphs: B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering is an interdisciplinary engineering discipline that addresses the technological modernization of agriculture and food production. Developed under the guidelines of ICAR and AICTE, the programme applies classical engineering disciplines—mechanical design, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and structural analysis—to agricultural production and value chains.

The curriculum spans four core pillars: Farm Machinery and Power Engineering (tractors, automated implements, robotic harvesting, agricultural drones), Soil and Water Conservation Engineering (watershed management, micro-irrigation, GIS, hydrological modeling), Agricultural Processing and Food Engineering (grain drying, cold chain storage, dairy processing, milling), and Renewable Energy Sources (biomass energy, solar pumping, bio-fuels).

During the four years, students acquire rigorous technical competencies in CAD design, workshop manufacturing, hydraulic circuits, digital sensor integration, and land surveying. In the final year, students complete a semester of in-plant industrial internship with farm machinery, irrigation, or food processing manufacturers under the Student READY scheme.

curriculum.heading: How the four years are organised
curriculum.intro: The course structure follows the national curriculum formulated by the ICAR Deans Committee for Agricultural Engineering. Course names and semester sequences may vary slightly across state agricultural universities and technological institutes.

structure.focus: Engineering mathematics, physics, mechanics, workshop technology, thermodynamics, surveying, and introductory agricultural sciences.
courses: Engineering mathematics and computational methods
Engineering mechanics and strength of materials
Workshop technology and manufacturing processes
Fluid mechanics and open channel hydraulics
Surveying and leveling for agricultural engineering
Thermodynamics, refrigeration, and air conditioning
Theory of machines and machine drawing (CAD)
Soil science and agronomic crop production basics

structure.focus: Tractors, tillage machinery, soil and water conservation, pressurized irrigation, crop processing, and renewable energy systems.
courses: Farm power and tractor systems
Farm machinery and equipment design
Soil and water conservation engineering
Pressurized irrigation systems (drip and sprinkler design)
Post-harvest engineering of cereals, pulses, and oilseeds
Dairy and food process engineering
Groundwater wells and pumping equipment
Renewable energy sources and biomass gasification

structure.focus: Precision farming, drone technology, industrial attachments, experiential learning, and major capstone design projects.
courses: Precision farming, remote sensing, and GIS applications
Agricultural drone operations and sensor telemetry
In-plant industrial training (tractor / implement / food / irrigation industry)
Experiential learning and product development project
Comprehensive viva-voce and seminar

practical_learning.name: In-Plant Industrial Attachment
practical_learning.description: Structured semester internship with tractor manufacturers, pump and micro-irrigation companies, food processing plants, or precision farming enterprises to gain hands-on industrial workflow experience.

practical_learning.name: Tractor & Implement Workshop Training
practical_learning.description: Practical engine overhaul, hydraulic diagnostic testing, laser land leveler operation, seed drill calibration, and combined harvester field operation.

practical_learning.name: Irrigation Design & Field Hydrology Labs
practical_learning.description: Hands-on survey and design of automated micro-irrigation networks, soil infiltration tests, contour bunding layout, and GIS watershed delineation.

points: Pass in 10+2 (Senior Secondary) examination with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics (PCM) from a recognised education board.
Candidates must have passed 10+2 with at least 50% marks in aggregate (40% for SC, ST, PwBD, and reserved category candidates for ICAR quota admissions).
Mathematics is compulsory for admission into B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering across all agricultural universities.
Candidates must have attained a minimum age of 16 years as of 31 August of the admission year for ICAR quota seats.

fees.summary: Tuition fees in state agricultural university engineering colleges are government-subsidised, ranging between ₹25,000 to ₹65,000 per year. In private universities and self-financing engineering institutes, tuition ranges from ₹90,000 to ₹2,50,000 annually. Hostel, workshop safety kits, and mess charges are payable separately.

careers.heading: Career pathways in engineering, technology, and governance
careers.intro: Agricultural engineers play a vital role in food security and environmental conservation. Demand has increased rapidly with the growth of precision agriculture, automated machinery, drone-based surveying, and commercial food supply chains.

roles.title: Design & R&D Engineer (Farm Machinery)
roles.description: Designs tractors, implements, automated seeders, and smart harvesters for agricultural equipment companies.

roles.title: Irrigation Systems Engineer
roles.description: Plans, calculates hydraulic layouts, and installs micro-irrigation, telemetry fertigation, and solar pumping networks.

roles.title: Food Process & Cold Chain Engineer
roles.description: Oversees grain elevators, fruit grading lines, dairy plants, and automated packaging systems.

roles.title: Agricultural Drone Specialist
roles.description: Manages drone telemetry, aerial crop health multispectral mapping, and automated pesticide spraying operations.

roles.title: Assistant Engineer (Irrigation / Agricultural Engineering)
roles.description: State government engineer managing watershed structures, farm mechanisation subsidies, and rural soil conservation projects.

roles.title: Technical Officer / Banking Agricultural Engineer
roles.description: Appraises agricultural machinery loans, warehouse infrastructure financing, and rural industrial projects in commercial banks.

faqs.question: Can biology students without Mathematics take B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering?
faqs.answer: No. Mathematics is a mandatory qualifying subject at the 10+2 level for B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering across all ICAR and AICTE-accredited universities.

faqs.question: Is B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering approved by AICTE as well as ICAR?
faqs.answer: Yes. Agricultural Engineering is a recognised engineering branch evaluated by both AICTE for technical engineering standards and ICAR for agricultural university affiliation.

faqs.question: What is the scope of GATE for Agricultural Engineering graduates?
faqs.answer: Graduates can appear for the GATE examination with the 'AG' (Agricultural Engineering) paper code. High scores qualify students for M.Tech. admissions at IIT Kharagpur, IIT Roorkee, and premier agricultural universities, as well as recruitment in selected public sector enterprises.

faqs.question: How does Agricultural Engineering differ from Mechanical Engineering?
faqs.answer: Mechanical Engineering focuses broadly on general machines, automobiles, and manufacturing. Agricultural Engineering applies mechanical principles directly to biological materials, soil mechanics, crop-machine interactions, micro-irrigation systems, and food processing.

faqs.question: Are agricultural engineers eligible for IT and general engineering roles?
faqs.answer: Yes. Students learn programming, CAD modeling, and data analytics, enabling many graduates to work in general engineering firms, software testing, GIS mapping companies, and technical consulting.
